judgements.reason: Bridge -> Reasoning. The `so_that` clause commits to a specific hybrid split ('local for coding / refactor / lint / test, remote only for long-horizon planning'), but the 2026-07-18 bridge (validation.3cab277c2cb7cb4c, dim=so_that) records the largest real-world instance of the hybrid harness arriving on a different axis: Anaconda's acquisition of Kilo Code, a gateway routing ~10 trillion tokens/month for 3 million developers across 500+ open-weight, self-hosted and frontier-cloud endpoints, where routing is driven by cost and governance policy rather than by task type. The bridge itself states 'the measurement runs against it'. The `because` and `given` clauses remain factually intact and the Q3 2026 landing window is still open, so this is a reframing, not a falsification: `so_that` should absorb the policy-routed-gateway variant of the hybrid harness alongside the task-type split, and `landing` should note that the Big-3 IDE local-first-toggle-as-default condition still has zero supporting evidence with ~10 weeks left while the cost shock the thesis predicted did arrive (Anthropic Fable 5 repricing, 2026-07-18).

All 16 bridges are internally coherent and correctly dimensioned, and the recent ones are honest about two-directional evidence rather than laundering it as support (2026-07-18 'the measurement runs against it'; 2026-06-04 'it cuts against the consumer-GPU framing'; 2026-05-01 'Mixed signal'). Relevance grading tracks that honesty (rel=2 on the oblique rows, rel=3-4 on the on-thesis ones). No bridge contradicts another and none misattributes its support_dimension. No rewrite warranted.

Bridge -> Needs. The Need-set models three actors and the week's evidence has split them apart. The consumer-GPU model-release actor (need.fe838d9eac86bc6a) has substantially delivered - Qwen3.6-27B, plus this week Bonsai 27B on a handset (2026-07-15), Kimi K3 (2026-07-17) and Qwen3.8 (2026-07-19) - so that Need should roll forward to its next precondition. The Big-3 IDE actor (need.b7248a8bd9e4a624) and the enterprise dev-platform actor (need.999a16eb965e14cd) have produced no evidence at all across the entire runway. Separately, the 2026-07-18 Kilo Code / Anaconda bridge surfaces an actor the Need-set does not model at all - the agent-gateway and governance vendor - which is the party actually moving 10 trillion tokens/month and applying the routing policy the prediction attributes to IDE vendors. Rewrite should re-cut the coalition around that fourth actor and re-window the surviving Needs into the Q3 2026 landing window (all three currently expire 2026-06-30, one day before the prediction's own target window opens).

DATA INCONSISTENCY - escalate, do not auto-fix. This prediction's relationship to prediction.bcace95fe3e753d1 is double-encoded in two mutually exclusive ways: prediction_relations row relation.d859cb06ef984cf8 records entails(a=prediction.82599b6cfd05751b, b=prediction.bcace95fe3e753d1), while prediction_chain simultaneously records bcace95fe3e753d1 -> 82599b6cfd05751b at strength 0.85. The prediction_relations schema comment forbids exactly this: 'if entails(A, B) exists, do NOT also write chain(A, B)'. The relation's own note ('the focal hybrid-harness claim presupposes the 27B Dense + 1M context standard becoming the on-prem default') describes an evidential precondition, not entailment by definition, so the chain edge is almost certainly the correct encoding and the entails row is the erroneous one - but choosing which to drop is a modelling decision for a human. Systemic: 12 of 14 entails relations in the DB are double-encoded this way, so a global fix is likely more appropriate than a per-prediction one. The remaining 3 chain edges and 6 relation edges on this prediction are well-formed.

Both antecedent clauses are historical facts that remain true: `because` (Unsloth v2026.5.26 shipped the selective-expert-checkpoint primitive, MiniMax M2.7 235B save footprint 470GB -> 188GB) and `given` (two independent 8x H200 SXM5 reproductions inside 3 percent). The consequent has until 2026-12-31 and this week's evidence increases rather than decreases the pressure behind it: Thinking Machines released Inkling on 2026-07-15 as a 975B-total / 41B-active MoE whose explicit business model is customer fine-tuning, and Unsloth shipped same-day support in v0.1.49-beta. Non-adoption by TRL / Axolotl / Llama-Factory so far is slow progress inside a generous window, not invalidation. No rewrite warranted.

All 5 bridges are correctly scoped and dimensioned, including the 2026-05-27 row that honestly reports a null result ('no fresh Hugging Face TRL, Axolotl, or Llama-Factory save-time primitive movement landed', dim=none, rel=3) rather than inventing support. The 2026-07-16 Inkling bridge correctly attaches to the cost mechanism (dim=because) rather than claiming adoption. No contradictions, no misattributions.

Bridge -> Reasoning, with the two streams moving in opposite directions. The `because` clause reads 'weights only promised in ~10 days' as a live commitment dated from the June 1 API-only launch, i.e. expected around June 11. It is now 2026-07-19, 38 days past that date, and today's own future-prediction verification states plainly that 'Nothing about MiniMax M3 appeared today and no rerun was published... there is no checkpoint to rerun.' Meanwhile both of this week's bridges strengthen the `given` clause by generalizing the hosted-API-first, weights-and-report-later pattern to two further labs (Kimi K3 on 2026-07-17 with weights promised July 27; Qwen3.8 on 2026-07-19 with weights promised undated). The reasoning needs reframing on two points: `because` should record that the 10-day promise elapsed unfulfilled rather than presenting it as pending, and `landing` should acknowledge that this is a conjunction whose binding risk has inverted - the failure mode is now that no checkpoint ships inside Q3 2026 at all, leaving the prediction unresolvable rather than wrong, since the rerun-comes-in-lower half cannot be tested without weights.

Both bridges are correctly scoped. Each is about a different lab than the named subject and each says so explicitly rather than overclaiming ('though the subject is Kimi, not MiniMax M3'; 'the generalization this rests on picks up a second lab'), and both are dimensioned to `given` - the structural force - rather than to `because`, which would have been the misattribution. Relevance 3 on both is proportionate to pattern-level rather than subject-level support. No rewrite warranted.

Both Needs remain genuinely open and correctly specified. The release-engineer Need (need.f39ff991311d6381, publish the M3 checkpoint and technical report) has not been delivered - no checkpoint exists as of today - and the evaluator Need (need.870b0a880fe5ffaa, rerun M3 on SWE-Bench Pro under a public harness) is strictly gated behind it. Both are windowed 2026-07-01..2026-09-30, exactly matching the prediction's own target window, so unlike several siblings in this batch there is no window defect here. Non-delivery inside an open window is the state the Need-set was written to describe; no rewrite warranted.

Bridge -> Reasoning, and this is the strongest staleness signal in the batch. The `so_that` clause claims 'Mistral / Meta / DeepSeek / Gemma converge on a 20-30B Dense x 1M context recipe and 70B+ MoE retreats to multimodal / tool / long-horizon niches'. Both halves ran into direct counter-evidence this week. On architecture, validation.4da3baa71b68ddbc (2026-07-16, dim=given, rel=2) records Inkling arriving as 975B-total / 41B-active MoE with 1M context and even Inkling-Small at 276B-total MoE - 'the newest headline open-weights slot again went to sparse architectures, not the dense mid-size shape the recipe requires' - and validation.c4ed70582c2e6c09 (2026-07-18, rel=2) calls Colibri 'the categorical opposite of this recipe', sparse and disk-resident rather than dense and VRAM-bound, noting 'the commodity VRAM floor the recipe anchors on stops binding'. Two further releases outside its bridges point the same way: Kimi K3 at 2.8T sparse MoE (2026-07-17) and Qwen3.8 at 2.4T (2026-07-19), the two largest announced open-weight models in the world, both sparse. On the retreat half, Inkling positions a 975B MoE as a fine-tunable enterprise base and Kimi K3 tops a coding arena - the MoE tier is expanding into coding and customization, not retreating from them. Separately the `landing` condition ('>=3 vendor 20-30B Dense releases') has been recorded as unmet by this prediction's own bridges continuously since 2026-04-24 with roughly ten weeks left. Reflected in the derived columns: this is the only prediction in the batch to fall to observed_relevance 2 / realization 0.4 while the other five hold at 3 / 0.6.

The bridge stream is performing correctly and needs no rewrite - it is the reason the reasoning staleness is detectable at all. Across 15 bridges the recent adverse rows are recorded as adverse in plain terms ('the categorical opposite of this recipe', 'counter-evidence on this forecast's architecture clause', 'running past the recipe rather than confirming it') and graded down to rel=2 accordingly, and the 2026-07-18 row is correctly dimensioned `none` rather than being forced onto a reasoning clause it does not support. Earlier rows likewise flagged the missing Mistral / Meta / Gemma releases inside their own windows. No misattribution, no contradiction between rows.
